errors.english: Just as the (Samkhya) an ancient school of Hindu philosophy proponents argue that if there is no difference, there are no distinct particulars and thus nothing can be established, so too the Buddhists argue that even if there is a difference, there are no distinct particulars
errors.why: This is the opponent's tu quoque against the Buddhist (just as for the Sāṃkhya non-difference makes no distinction so that not everything is a producer, so too for the Buddhist difference makes no distinction), not a position the Sāṃkhyas and Buddhists each 'argue'; the next sentence asks for the reply to it.

fix.find: Just as the (Samkhya) an ancient school of Hindu philosophy proponents argue that if there is no difference, there are no distinct particulars and thus nothing can be established, so too the Buddhists argue that even if there is a difference, there are no distinct particulars
fix.replace: [Objection:] Just as for the Sāṃkhya (an ancient school of Hindu philosophy), if non-difference makes no distinction, not everything is a producer, so too for the Buddhists, if difference makes no distinction, [the same follows]

errors.english: or for it not to apprehend its own nature
errors.why: The point is that it is unreasonable for the universal's own form not to be grasped (by cognition), not that the universal itself fails to apprehend.

note: Follows the commentary's glosses reasonably, but turns the opponent's Sāṃkhya/Buddhist parity objection into a statement of what both schools argue.

errors.english: Make offerings and praise the chosen deity.
errors.why: The phrase continues མེ་ from the previous side: 'offer to the fire god (me yi lha) and praise him', in the homa context, not the chosen deity.

fix.find: Make offerings and praise the chosen deity
fix.replace: Make offerings to the fire deity and praise him

errors.english: should purify through confession and the mandala offering
errors.why: མ་བཤགས reads 'without confession': a yogin of little capacity, not doing confession, should purify by means of the maṇḍala.

note: A generally sound rendering of the colophon verses and the new samaya-purification text, with the fire god misread as the chosen deity.

errors.english: one can walk a hundred yojanas and back
errors.why: brgya stong is a hundred thousand yojanas, not a hundred.

fix.find: one can walk a hundred yojanas and back
fix.replace: one can walk a hundred thousand yojanas and back

errors.english: recites the vidyāmantra one hundred thousand times at the door of the house
errors.why: stong phrag brgyad is eight thousand recitations.

fix.find: recites the vidyāmantra one hundred thousand times at the door of the house
fix.replace: recites the vidyāmantra eight thousand times at the door of the house

errors.english: If one makes an effigy from rice flour and smears it with the powder, the target will be afflicted with leprosy.
errors.why: The Tibetan has two separate rice-flour effigy rites: the first makes the enemy paralysed (rengs pa), the second gives leprosy; the first is dropped.

fix.find: If one makes an effigy from rice flour
fix.replace: If one makes an effigy from rice flour and smears it with the powder, that enemy will become paralyzed. If one makes an effigy from rice flour

errors.english: If one gives the powder to an enemy
errors.why: The powder is first mixed with excrement before being given to the enemy.

fix.find: If one gives the powder to an enemy
fix.replace: If one mixes the powder with excrement and gives it to an enemy

errors.english: one will be separated from that enemy
errors.why: The result is that the enemies are divided (set against one another), not that the practitioner is separated from the enemy.

note: Readable, but two numbers are wrong, two rites are dropped or truncated, and one result is misattributed.

errors.english: One is desired to be liberated.
errors.why: The verse says that because the mind is freed, he (the teacher) holds these to be liberations (vimokṣa), not that someone is desired to be liberated.

errors.english:
Are adorned with the precious wheel, the lotus,
The sword, and the eight pillars.
errors.why: Wheel, jewel, lotus and sword are the emblems marking the eight pillars (the eight liberations), so the list is mis-segmented, with the jewel merged into 'precious wheel' and the pillars made a fourth item.

note: A faithful verse rendering of the eight liberations and palace symbolism, with two obscure lines misconstrued.

errors.english: the character of the process in this [note: Madhyamaka or Middle Way] system
errors.why: འདིའི here means 'of this' eight-qualified dependent origination (contrasted with the twelve links), not 'this Madhyamaka system'.

note: The argument contrasting eight-qualified dependent origination with the twelve links is rendered accurately.

errors.english: Thirdly, one should meditate on the fire mandala, which is red,
errors.why: གསུམ་པ completes ཟུར་ from the previous side: the fire maṇḍala is 'three-cornered' (triangular), not 'thirdly'.

fix.find: Thirdly, one should meditate on the fire mandala, which is red
fix.replace: One should meditate on the fire mandala, which is triangular and red

note: Accurate commentary on the inner homa maṇḍalas, apart from the triangular fire maṇḍala misread as an ordinal.

errors.why: Dgongs pa lung ston/bstan is the title of the Sandhivyākaraṇa Tantra; the invented Sanskrit and descriptive rendering misidentify the cited text.

fix.replace: the Revelation of the Intent [note: the Sandhivyākaraṇa Tantra]

errors.why: phrin las is the Tibetan word (Sanskrit karman/kṛtya); the note mislabels it as Sanskrit.

note: The bhūmi list and the word commentary are rendered soundly; the cited tantra is misidentified.
A faithful verse translation of the Svastigāthā refrains and the Three Jewels stanzas.

errors.english: is stated starting from the point of permanently abandoning the aggregate of form, up to the point of what is called "thorough knowledge,"
errors.why: The citation runs from '[the form aggregate] is posited as svalakṣaṇa or viśeṣalakṣaṇa' up to 'the form aggregate is permanently abandoned and thoroughly known as svalakṣaṇa or viśeṣalakṣaṇa', so the abandoning belongs to the end of the range, not its start.

note: A sound Abhidharma-style commentary rendering, with the opening cross-reference to the sūtra garbled.
A faithful rendering of the añjana rite and the Dīpaṃkara/Śākyamuni non-difference gloss.
